action.description: Establish initial performance model, constraints, and first alternative kernel directions for the fused one-launch HIP MoE kernel.
action.rationale: A correct world model is required before implementing mutually exclusive ownership/mapping strategies under strict single-kernel constraints.
action.title: Initialize world model and branch candidates

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: MI300X/CDNA3 favors wave64-coherent work, MFMA-friendly K/N tiling, and careful VGPR/LDS balance.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Problem has GEMM-like arithmetic but dynamic expert indirection can break regular MFMA utilization.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Irregular routing may lower achieved matrix-core occupancy.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Weight traffic dominates unless expert reuse is exploited; input/topk metadata is comparatively small.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Low seq_len or high expert dispersion can make kernel bandwidth/latency bound.

register_pressure.notes: Need fp32 accumulation for numerical stability; output tile + intermediates can quickly consume VGPRs.
register_pressure.risk: Over-tiling may collapse occupancy on MI300X.

nodes.notes:
- 1) Problem classification: fused dynamic-sparse MoE kernel combining routing, FP8 block-dequant, FC1(4096), SiLU*up, FC2(7168), topk(4) weighted combine, and BF16 writeback in exactly one custom HIP launch; dense output but sparse/indirect expert access.
- 2) Canonical math: for token t, y_t = sum_{k=0..3} a_{t,k} * (W2[e_{t,k}]^T * (silu(g_{t,k}) ⊙ u_{t,k})); [g,u] = W1[e_{t,k}]^T * x_t; x_t uses per-token block scales, W1/W2 use per-expert block scales; reductions over hidden/intermediate dims, route contributions independent except same-token accumulation.
- 3) Data layout/access: input_q[T,7168] fp8 + input_scale[T,56] fp32 (contiguous token-major); w1_q[32,4096,7168] fp8 + fc1_scale[32,1792]; w2_q[32,7168,2048] fp8 + fc2_scale[32,896]; topk_ids/topk_weights [T,4] indirect; dominant reads are W1/W2, writes are output[T,7168] bf16.
- 4) Regime hypotheses: (A) small T => launch/latency + under-occupancy bottleneck; (B) medium/large T with balanced experts => compute/VGPR pressure bottleneck if MFMA utilization good; (C) skewed routing/hot experts => load-imbalance and potential combine contention bottleneck.
- 5) Kernel knobs: ownership mapping (token/expert/route tile), output and K tiling, on-the-fly dequant granularity, route traversal order, accumulation precision, synchronization/atomic strategy, persistent-CTA vs direct grid.
- 6) High-level skeleton: read token topk ids/weights; iterate selected experts; stream W1 tiles with block scales -> stage1; apply SiLU*up; stream W2 tiles with block scales -> stage2; apply route weight; accumulate token output fp32; final bf16 store. Sync points depend on ownership strategy.
- 7) Candidate families (pruned): token-major output-stationary, expert-major persistent, and hybrid route-major split-output; each targets different reuse/load-balance tradeoffs under one-launch/no-aux-kernel constraints.

action.description: Build a single-kernel token-owned path where each workgroup owns token output tiles and processes its 4 routed experts sequentially with fp32 accumulation before bf16 writeback.
action.rationale: Simplest way to satisfy one-launch + no-aux-kernel + exact combine semantics without cross-CTA reductions.
action.title: Alternative A: Token-major output-stationary fused kernel

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Wave64-friendly if hidden/output tiles align to MFMA shapes; no inter-CTA reduction improves scheduling simplicity.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Good correctness path; compute efficiency depends on whether per-token expert diversity harms weight locality.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: May underutilize matrix cores when T is small or routing is highly random.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Can reread large W1/W2 slabs for each token-route; weak inter-token weight reuse unless cache captures hot experts.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Bandwidth pressure from repeated weight fetches can dominate.

register_pressure.notes: Output-stationary fp32 accumulators plus FC1/FC2 fragments are heavy; requires conservative tile sizing.
register_pressure.risk: VGPR growth may reduce occupancy and hide less memory latency.

nodes.notes: Best first implementation for correctness/perf bring-up under strict single-launch constraints; avoids atomics by keeping token ownership local. SELF_CHECK: cannot be combined with sibling expert-major/hybrid ownership in the same plan because ownership and reduction semantics are mutually exclusive.

action.description: Build a single-kernel persistent expert-owned path that internally discovers/iterates token routes for each expert to maximize W1/W2 reuse and computes FC1+act+FC2 before combining.
action.rationale: Maximizes expert weight reuse, which is critical because W1/W2 traffic is dominant at these dimensions.
action.title: Alternative B: Expert-major persistent fused kernel

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Potentially better MFMA residency due to repeated tiles from the same expert; persistent scheduling may match MI300X throughput behavior.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Higher arithmetic intensity from weight reuse when many tokens map to same expert.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: In-kernel routing discovery/control flow can reduce SIMD efficiency.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Best chance to amortize expert weight loads across multiple tokens/routes.
memory_bandwidth.risk: If routing is uniform but sparse per expert at small T, reuse advantage collapses.

register_pressure.notes: State for expert queues, partial outputs, and dequant fragments can be substantial.
register_pressure.risk: May force smaller tiles and extra synchronization.

nodes.notes: Performance-oriented direction for large T with reusable experts; correctness is harder due to dynamic route handling entirely inside one kernel. SELF_CHECK: cannot be combined with token-owned sibling because both define incompatible primary ownership/reduction paths.

action.description: Build a single-kernel route-major split-output path where workgroups process (token,expert,slot) route tiles and accumulate weighted FC2 partials into output tiles with controlled atomic or partitioned reduction.
action.rationale: Balances dynamic routing flexibility and parallelism when token-major underutilizes hardware or expert-major suffers imbalance.
action.title: Alternative C: Hybrid route-major split-output fused kernel

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Can preserve wave64 occupancy via many independent route tiles; MFMA use depends on tile regularity per route.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: More parallel scheduling flexibility than strict token/expert ownership.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Combine phase may serialize if many routes hit same output regions.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Intermediate locality is moderate; better than pure token-major in some skew cases but worse than expert-major reuse.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Atomic write traffic can inflate memory system pressure.

register_pressure.notes: Can keep smaller per-workgroup state by splitting output, reducing peak accumulator footprint.
register_pressure.risk: Additional bookkeeping for route/output partitioning increases control overhead.

nodes.notes: Middle-ground branch for uneven expert loads and larger grids; may trade deterministic accumulation simplicity for parallelism. SELF_CHECK: cannot be combined with siblings because it relies on split-output ownership and explicit cross-route combination semantics.

kernel_summary: This is a fused, single-launch dynamic MoE kernel on MI300X that must perform in one HIP kernel: route read/dispatch (topk=4), FP8 block-scaled dequantized FC1 (4096), SiLU×up activation (2048), FP8 block-scaled FC2 (7168), weighted topk combine, and final BF16 writeback, with no auxiliary kernels or ATen matmul-family calls. The math is GEMM-like but with sparse indirect expert selection per token, so dominant cost is W1/W2 movement unless expert reuse is captured; likely bottlenecks vary by seq_len and routing skew between memory-latency/bandwidth limits (small or dispersed workloads) and compute/VGPR occupancy limits (large balanced workloads). Key constraints strongly favor ownership strategies that preserve correctness without cross-kernel staging while respecting HIP integration rules (host wrappers in main.cpp, real launch in kernel.cu).
open_questions: What is the real seq_len distribution at runtime (e.g., 1-32, 128-1K, >4K), and must one kernel configuration serve all efficiently?
How skewed are topk expert assignments in production (uniform vs hot experts), and what is the per-expert token histogram variance?
Are output accumulation determinism or strict reproducibility requirements present, or is non-deterministic atomic accumulation acceptable within tolerance?
What numerical error budget is allowed versus the torch reference (fp32 accumulation depth, activation precision, bf16 cast timing)?
Can we assume w1_q/w2_q and scales are persistent across many invocations (enabling cache-friendly expert-major behavior), or do they change frequently?
What MI300X kernel resource limits are acceptable for this op (target occupancy floor, max VGPR/thread, max LDS/block) under deployment constraints?
Is backward/gradient support irrelevant for this kernel path (inference-only), allowing aggressive forward-only specialization?
